heroHeadline: PM Fils-Aimé Declares August Elections Impossible; West Department Violence Toll Rises to 80+ Dead — MSF Cité Soleil Hospital Remains Closed Day 5
heroSubtitle: On May 12, 2026, Prime Minister Alix Didier Fils-Aimé declared on Magik9 radio that 'it is clear that the security conditions are not met at the level for us to have elections in August' — the first explicit abandonment of the August 30 election date by the transitional government itself — announcing a revised target of end of 2026 elections with a new president by February 2027. The declaration followed the worst Port-au-Prince security deterioration since the February–March 2024 gang offensive: HaitiLibre's May 14 Zapping roundup reported a cumulative toll of 80+ dead and 100+ wounded from the sustained gang fighting that erupted across Cité Soleil, the Cul-de-Sac Plain, and surrounding West Department zones beginning May 10. IOM ETT #93 and OCHA Flash Update No. 1 issued formal humanitarian alerts on May 13. MSF's Cité Soleil hospital — the only emergency medical facility for the commune's 300,000+ residents — remained closed for a fifth consecutive day as of May 14–15, with no public timeline for reopening. The Centre Hospitalier de Fontaine also remained suspended. A Washington Post investigation published May 15 found the US has spent approximately $970 million on Haiti security since 2024, yet gang control of Port-au-Prince expanded from 80% to 90% during the 22-month MSS mission. The GSF advance force of approximately 545 personnel continues to operate exclusively in Port-au-Prince city center, leaving Cité Soleil and the entire Artibonite Department without international security coverage. A UN News feature documented Haiti's media collapse — 14 journalists killed since 2021, Le Nouvelliste forced online-only, two sports journalists murdered in May 2026. No electoral decree has been issued; voter registration has not begun; 23 communes remain inaccessible. 1.47M+ Haitians internally displaced; 5.9M face acute food insecurity; the 2026 HRP funded at only ~20% of its $880M target.
